```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)

escape_html <- function(x) {
  x <- ifelse(is.na(x) | !nzchar(as.character(x)), "—", as.character(x))
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub('"', "&quot;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}

format_effect <- function(estimate, lower, upper) {
  sprintf("SMD %.2f<br><span class='subtle'>(%.2f to %.2f)</span>",
          estimate, lower, upper)
}

format_probability <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "—", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x))
}

format_domain <- function(label, rationale = NA_character_, diagnostic = NULL) {
  text <- escape_html(label)
  details <- character()
  if (!is.null(diagnostic) && nzchar(diagnostic)) {
    details <- c(details, escape_html(diagnostic))
  }
  if (!is.na(rationale) && nzchar(rationale)) {
    details <- c(details, escape_html(rationale))
  }
  if (length(details)) {
    paste0(
      text, "<details><summary>Basis</summary><span class='subtle'>",
      paste(details, collapse = "<br>"), "</span></details>"
    )
  } else {
    text
  }
}

make_grade_table <- function(data) {
  outcome_order <- names(outcome_labels)
  data <- data |>
    arrange(
      factor(outcome, levels = outcome_order),
      resistance_exercise_code,
      contrast_family_order,
      protein_intake_proposed
    )
  html <- c(
    "<div class='grade-scroll'><table class='grade-table'>",
    "<thead>",
    paste0(
      "<tr><th rowspan='2'>Contrast</th>",
      "<th colspan='7'>Certainty assessment</th>",
      "<th colspan='4'>Summary of findings</th></tr>"
    ),
    paste0(
      "<tr><th>Evidence base</th><th>Study design</th>",
      "<th>Risk of bias</th><th>Inconsistency</th>",
      "<th>Indirectness</th><th>Imprecision</th>",
      "<th>Publication bias / other</th><th>Effect (95% CrI)</th>",
      "<th>Decision probabilities</th><th>Certainty</th>",
      "<th>Importance</th></tr>"
    ),
    "</thead><tbody>"
  )
  group_keys <- data |>
    distinct(outcome, rt_condition)
  for (group_index in seq_len(nrow(group_keys))) {
    outcome_name <- group_keys$outcome[[group_index]]
    rt_name <- group_keys$rt_condition[[group_index]]
    rows <- data |>
      filter(outcome == outcome_name, rt_condition == rt_name)
    html <- c(
      html,
      sprintf(
        "<tr class='group-row'><td colspan='12'>%s — %s</td></tr>",
        escape_html(outcome_labels[[outcome_name]]),
        escape_html(rt_name)
      )
    )
    family_keys <- rows |>
      distinct(contrast_family_order, contrast_family) |>
      arrange(contrast_family_order)
    for (family_index in seq_len(nrow(family_keys))) {
      family_name <- family_keys$contrast_family[[family_index]]
      family_rows <- rows |>
        filter(contrast_family == family_name)
      html <- c(
        html,
        sprintf(
          "<tr class='family-row'><td colspan='12'>%s</td></tr>",
          escape_html(family_name)
        )
      )
      for (row_index in seq_len(nrow(family_rows))) {
        row <- family_rows[row_index, ]
      evidence <- sprintf(
        paste0(
          "%d studies; %s participants<span class='subtle'>%d arms; ",
          "%d studies strictly span both dose endpoints</span>"
        ),
        row$studies,
        format(row$participants, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
        row$arms,
        row$studies_spanning_contrast
      )
      rob_diagnostic <- sprintf(
        "RoB 2: %d low / %d some concerns / %d high",
        row$low, row$some_concerns, row$high
      )
      inconsistency_diagnostic <- sprintf(
        "DI %.1f%%; ASI %.1f%%; %s",
        row$DI, row$ASI, row$inconsistency_suggestion
      )
      imprecision_diagnostic <- sprintf(
        "Automated threshold flag: %s",
        row$imprecision_suggestion
      )
      publication_diagnostic <- sprintf(
        "Unadjusted %.2f; RoBMA-adjusted %.2f",
        row$estimate_brma, row$estimate_robma
      )
      probabilities <- sprintf(
        "Gain at higher intake %s<br>Equivalent %s<br>Loss at higher intake %s",
        format_probability(row$probability_benefit),
        format_probability(row$probability_equivalence),
        format_probability(row$probability_detriment)
      )
      certainty <- sprintf(
        "<span class='certainty-symbols'>%s</span><br>%s",
        escape_html(row$certainty_symbols),
        escape_html(row$certainty)
      )
      support_note <- if (isTRUE(row$supported)) {
        "Within displayed outcome/RT range"
      } else {
        paste("Model-based extrapolation:", row$support_status)
      }
      effect <- paste0(
        format_effect(row$estimate, row$lower_95, row$upper_95),
        "<span class='subtle'>", escape_html(support_note), "</span>"
      )
      html <- c(
        html,
        "<tr>",
        sprintf("<td class='left'>%s</td>", escape_html(row$contrast_label)),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", evidence),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", escape_html(row$study_design)),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", format_domain(
          row$risk_of_bias, row$risk_of_bias_rationale, rob_diagnostic
        )),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", format_domain(
          row$inconsistency,
          row$inconsistency_rationale,
          inconsistency_diagnostic
        )),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", format_domain(
          row$indirectness, row$indirectness_rationale,
          sprintf("%d/%d studies strictly span both endpoints; observed %.2f–%.2f",
                  row$studies_spanning_contrast, row$studies,
                  row$observed_min_empirical, row$observed_max_empirical)
        )),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", format_domain(
          row$imprecision, row$imprecision_rationale,
          imprecision_diagnostic
        )),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", format_domain(
          row$publication_bias,
          row$publication_bias_rationale,
          publication_diagnostic
        )),
        sprintf("<td class='effect'>%s</td>", effect),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", probabilities),
        sprintf("<td class='certainty'>%s</td>", certainty),
        sprintf("<td>%s</td>", escape_html(row$importance)),
        "</tr>"
      )
      }
    }
  }
  paste(c(html, "</tbody></table></div>"), collapse = "\n")
}
```

# Scope

This GRADE appraisal is restricted to the preregistered primary analyses of
body-mass-relative protein intake. It does not include the exploratory absolute
intake or supplementation models. Two fixed-reference contrast families are
reported for RT:

- 1.2, 1.6, 2.0, and 2.4 versus 0.8 g/kg/day; and
- 2.0 upward in 0.4-g/kg/day increments versus 1.6 g/kg/day, stopping at
  4.4 for whole-body lean/fat-free mass, 2.4 for measures of muscle size or mass,
  and 3.2 for strength and physical function.

The 1.6-reference ceilings are the highest 0.4-g/kg/day increments within the
pooled observed range for each outcome. For No RT, proposed intakes are
restricted to the outcome-specific observed maximum. On the planned
0.4-g/kg/day grid, each outcome therefore contributes only 1.2 and 1.6 versus
0.8 g/kg/day in the No-RT stratum; all proposed intakes of 2.0 g/kg/day or
higher exceed the No-RT maxima of approximately 1.80–1.82 g/kg/day and are not
reported.

The unit of appraisal is an outcome, resistance-training condition, and dose
contrast. Population effects come from the complete primary 26-model stacking
ensemble. The inconsistency analysis uses the same primary evidence but
re-stacks the 12 candidate models per outcome that permit study-specific dose
slopes or smooths.

```{r}
      "illustrative and must not be interpreted as study results.</div>"
    )

}
```

# Evidence profile

The table follows the structure of a GRADE Summary of Findings table while
adapting the participant columns to a continuous dose-response analysis. The
same participants can inform several dose contrasts and cannot be partitioned
into fixed “higher” and “habitual” groups for every model-derived comparison.
Select **Basis** within a domain cell to read the rationale and any accompanying diagnostic.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grade-profile
#| results: asis

cat(make_grade_table(profile))
```

# Population effects and imprecision

The effect is the model-averaged difference in standardised mean change at the
proposed intake versus the stated 0.8- or 1.6-g/kg/day reference. Positive
values favour the proposed higher intake. The preregistered smallest effect
size of interest is ±0.10 SMD.

The automated imprecision flag asks whether the 95% posterior interval remains
within one decision region, crosses one SESOI boundary, or crosses both the
lower and upper SESOI boundaries. It is evidence for—rather than a replacement
for—the final GRADE judgment.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-population-effects
#| tbl-cap: "Primary population-average contrasts and threshold-based imprecision diagnostics."

profile |>
  transmute(
    Outcome = outcome_label,
    Condition = rt_condition,
    Family = contrast_family,
    Contrast = contrast_label,
    `SMD estimate` = round(estimate, 3),
    `Lower 95% CrI` = round(lower_95, 3),
    `Upper 95% CrI` = round(upper_95, 3),
    `P(gain at higher intake)` = round(probability_benefit, 3),
    `P(equivalence)` = round(probability_equivalence, 3),
    `P(loss at higher intake)` = round(probability_detriment, 3),
    Conclusion = dplyr::recode(
      posterior_conclusion,
      "meaningful benefit" = "meaningful gain at higher intake",
      "meaningful detriment" = "meaningful loss at higher intake"
    ),
    `Automated imprecision flag` = imprecision_suggestion,
    `Observed-range support` = support_status
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", rep("r", 6), "l", "l", "l"))
```

# Inconsistency

For study $j$, inconsistency is assessed for the latent study-specific
contrast

$$
\Delta_j(d,r)=f_j(d)-f_j(r), \qquad r \in \{0.8,1.6\}.
$$

Posterior draws were generated with the same study, arm, and outcome
identifiers at both dose endpoints. Consequently, study-, arm-, and
outcome-level random intercepts cancel; only study-specific variation in the
dose association contributes to the contrast. Sampling error was not added to
these latent expected effects.

The Decision Inconsistency index (DI) and Across-Studies Inconsistency index
(ASI) follow Sousa-Pinto et al. [-@sousaPintoQuantitativeAssessment2025].
DI describes dispersion across the three SESOI decision categories. ASI
describes whether decision-category distributions systematically differ by
study. Values of DI ≥50% or ASI ≥25% prompted closer examination of unexplained
inconsistency before the domain judgment was recorded.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inconsistency
#| tbl-cap: "Decision-threshold inconsistency diagnostics for study-specific dose contrasts."

inconsistency |>
  mutate(
    Outcome = unname(outcome_labels[outcome]),
    Condition = if_else(resistance_exercise_code == 0, "RT", "No RT"),
    Family = contrast_family,
    Contrast = sprintf(
      "%.1f versus %.1f",
      protein_intake_proposed,
      protein_intake_reference
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Outcome,
    Condition,
    Family,
    Contrast,
    `Contributing studies` = studies,
    `Studies strictly spanning both endpoints` =
      directly_spanning_studies,
    `DI (%)` = round(DI, 1),
    `ASI (%)` = round(ASI, 1),
    `Strictly spanning studies DI (%)` = round(direct_support_DI, 1),
    `Strictly spanning studies ASI (%)` = round(direct_support_ASI, 1),
    `Median study SD` = round(study_sd_median, 3),
    Suggestion = inconsistency_suggestion
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", rep("r", 7), "l")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-inconsistency-profile
#| fig-cap: "DI and ASI profiles as proposed protein intake increases from the fixed 0.8- and 1.6-g/kg/day references. Horizontal dashed lines show the published values suggested as prompts for important unexplained inconsistency."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8

inconsistency |>
  mutate(
    Outcome = factor(
      unname(outcome_labels[outcome]),
      levels = unname(outcome_labels)
    ),
    Condition = if_else(resistance_exercise_code == 0, "RT", "No RT"),
    Reference = sprintf("%.1f reference", protein_intake_reference)
  ) |>
  select(
    Outcome, Condition, Reference,
    protein_intake_proposed, DI, ASI
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(DI, ASI), names_to = "Index", values_to = "Percent") |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = protein_intake_proposed,
    y = Percent,
    colour = Index,
    linetype = Reference,
    group = interaction(Index, Reference)
  )) +
  geom_hline(
    data = tibble(Index = c("DI", "ASI"), threshold = c(50, 25)),
    aes(yintercept = threshold, colour = Index),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.45,
    show.legend = FALSE,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_grid(Outcome ~ Condition) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1.2, 4.4, by = 0.4)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(DI = "#9c4a36", ASI = "#26789a")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Proposed protein intake (g/kg/day)",
    y = "Index (%)",
    colour = NULL,
    linetype = "Contrast family"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Influence and empirical support

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inconsistency-influence
#| tbl-cap: "Ranges of DI and ASI after omitting each study in turn."

inconsistency_loo |>
  group_by(
    outcome, resistance_exercise_code,
    contrast_family,
    protein_intake_reference, protein_intake_proposed
  ) |>
  summarise(
    min_DI = min(DI),
    max_DI = max(DI),
    min_ASI = min(ASI),
    max_ASI = max(ASI),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Outcome = unname(outcome_labels[outcome]),
    Condition = if_else(resistance_exercise_code == 0, "RT", "No RT"),
    Family = contrast_family,
    Contrast = sprintf(
      "%.1f versus %.1f",
      protein_intake_proposed,
      protein_intake_reference
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Outcome,
    Condition,
    Family,
    Contrast,
    `LOO DI range (%)` = sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", min_DI, max_DI),
    `LOO ASI range (%)` = sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", min_ASI, max_ASI)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "r"))
```

Study-specific predictions at target doses outside a study’s observed dose
range are partially pooled model-based estimates. The primary DI/ASI analysis
includes all contributing studies. A strict direct-support sensitivity is
therefore also shown when at least two studies have a within-study
achieved-intake range that brackets both dose endpoints. Each study is counted
once regardless of its number of arms; no tolerance is applied to this strict
spanning definition. Absence of strictly spanning studies is not interpreted
as evidence of consistency.

The complete study-level estimates and support flags are provided in
`inconsistency_study_summary.csv.gz` alongside this report’s analytic bundle.

# Risk of bias

The [risk-of-bias supplement](risk-of-bias.html) reports RoB 2 judgments for one
prespecified index result per trial. These judgments inform the risk-of-bias
assessment for the broader dose-response evidence.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rob2-grade
#| tbl-cap: "RoB 2 judgments among studies contributing to each outcome and resistance-training condition."

rob2 |>
  mutate(
    Outcome = unname(outcome_labels[outcome]),
    Condition = if_else(resistance_exercise_code == 0, "RT", "No RT")
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Outcome,
    Condition,
    `Contributing studies` = contributing_studies,
    Assessed = assessed_studies,
    Low = low,
    `Some concerns` = some_concerns,
    High = high,
    `Unassessed study numbers` = na_if(
      as.character(unassessed_study_numbers),
      ""
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "l", rep("r", 5), "l"))
```

# Publication bias

Publication-bias evidence is outcome-level and is applied consistently across
RT strata and target contrasts unless reviewers record a justified exception.
The [publication-bias supplement](publication-bias.html) reports comparisons of
matched unadjusted Bayesian random-effects and publication-bias-adjusted robust
Bayesian model-averaged analyses.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-publication-bias-grade
#| tbl-cap: "Outcome-level publication-bias model summaries used in the GRADE appraisal."

publication_bias |>
  mutate(Outcome = unname(outcome_labels[outcome])) |>
  transmute(
    Outcome,
    `Independent publication units` = publication_units,
    `Unadjusted estimate` = round(estimate_brma, 3),
    `Unadjusted 95% interval` = sprintf(
      "%.3f to %.3f", lower_95_brma, upper_95_brma
    ),
    `RoBMA-adjusted estimate` = round(estimate_robma, 3),
    `RoBMA 95% interval` = sprintf(
      "%.3f to %.3f", lower_95_robma, upper_95_robma
    ),
    `Adjusted minus unadjusted` = round(adjusted_minus_unadjusted, 3)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

# Indirectness

Indirectness is judged separately for each contrast. Relevant considerations
include whether both target doses fall within the outcome/RT-specific observed
range, how many unique studies have a within-study achieved-intake range that
strictly brackets both endpoints, reliance on overlapping shorter dose
intervals, applicability of the populations and outcomes, and the fact that
the primary estimand concerns achieved rather than precisely assigned protein
intake. These diagnostics do not themselves dictate a downgrade.

# From domain judgments to overall certainty

Overall certainty combines the recorded domain judgments in
`data/GRADE/grade_domain_judgments.csv`. The evidence profile reports the
rationales alongside the analytical diagnostics.

No automatic upgrade is applied for a dose-response gradient. Any proposed
upgrade must be explicitly recorded and justified after considering analytic
credibility, residual confounding, ecological bias, and consistency of the
gradient.

# Model contribution and audit trail

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inconsistency-weights
#| tbl-cap: "Restricted stacking weights for study-varying dose-effect candidates."

weights |>
  mutate(Outcome = unname(outcome_labels[outcome])) |>
  transmute(
    Outcome,
    `Model index` = model_index,
    Model = model_name,
    `Restricted stacking weight` = round(restricted_stacking_weight, 4),
    `LOO source` = loo_source
  ) |>
  filter(`Restricted stacking weight` > 0) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "r", "l", "r", "l"))
```

All analytic inputs passed the pipeline preflight:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grade-preflight

preflight |>
  transmute(Check = check, Passed = passed, Detail = detail) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "c", "l"))
```

The durable analysis bundle includes population contrasts, empirical-support
counts, study-specific latent effects, DI/ASI results, leave-one-study-out
analyses, RoB 2 summaries, publication-bias summaries, a snapshot of reviewer
decisions, the completed evidence profile, and checksums for all files.
